newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: ASEAN officials arrive in Cambodia for talks.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN officials arrive in Cambodia for talks.

text.p: Top ASEAN representatives arrived in Phnom Penh on Monday to formally notify Cambodia of its acceptance into the regional group in July along with Burma and Laos, officials said.

Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Secretary-General Ajit Singh and Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi were also expected to discuss preparations for Cambodia's entry into the club, officials and diplomats said.
"We will study various procedures and discuss what needs to be done," Badawi told reporters after arriving at Pochentong Airport with Singh.
Analysts and diplomats said Cambodia's political instability would also be a likely topic of discussion.
"Privately, they will inform (Cambodia) politely but firmly that when they are members of ASEAN, they need to adhere to certain behaviour in line with other ASEAN countries," one ASEAN diplomat said.
"They will be telling them indirectly that they should shape up."
Badawi and Singh, who are on a tour of the new member countries, were scheduled to meet co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, Foreign Minister Ung Huot and acting Head of State Chea Sim.
ASEAN last month agreed to admit Cambodia, Burma and Laos at its annual meeting in Kuala Lumpur in July.

ASEAN, which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, decided to admit the three despite Western pressure to deny Burma membership because of its human rights record and concerns over political instability in Cambodia.
Relations between Ranariddh and Hun Sen have plummeted in the run-up to next year's general elections.

Their increasingly acrimonious relationship has caused considerable tension in the capital and deadlocked the National Assembly, which has been unable to convene to pass key legislation needed for ASEAN membership.
Badawi and Singh return to Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
